subject: Access gating & procurement checklist for Skyline sandbox
messages:
From: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@skylinebank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@skylinebank.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Access gating & procurement checklist for Skyline sandbox

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team asked me to confirm a few items before we sign the contract:

- SSO: We need SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated support and metadata exchange. Can you confirm your ACS endpoints and certificate rotation cadence?
- SCIM: Confirmed? We want group sync (2-way) for the 3 environment groups (admins, engineers, auditors). Any rate limit notes?
- IP allowlists: We prefer an allowlist for production but want a staging fallback so the integration team can test from our CI runners (35.190.0.0/16). Do you support per-environment allowlists?
- Service accounts: Our infra team needs guidance on naming, scopes, and whether Redwood provides short-lived credentials or expects long-lived keys.
- Org policies & data residency: checklist for audit evidence (logs, retention, SOC support items).

Procurement (Sarah) is copied — she handles the SLA/redline items. We’d like a short mutual action plan (MAP) by EOD Wednesday so legal can start redlines. Can you put together a pre-flight checklist and estimate how long the SSO+SCIM cutover usually takes for banks of our size?

Thanks,
Clara
--
Clara Ruiz
Director, Identity & Access (Cloud Platforms)
Skyline Bank
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@skylinebank.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@skylinebank.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access gating & procurement checklist for Skyline sandbox

Hi Clara —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front and a plan below. I’m looping in Monica (Customer Success lead) and Ben (Solutions / implementations) to draft the MAP and technical pre-flight.

Short answers:
- SSO/SAML: ACS endpoints and SAML metadata are attached. Certificate rotation is quarterly by default; we can move to monthly with notification.
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 with group-sync. Default rate limit for orgs your size is 600 requests/min; we can request a bump for the initial sync window.
- IP allowlists: Yes, per-environment allowlists are supported. We can add the CI block as a staging fallback.
- Service accounts: Redwood recommends short-lived tokens with delegated scopes; we will provide a provisioning pattern and naming guide.
- Org policies / audit: We’ll attach a checklist for the evidence items (audit logs, retention windows, KMS integration notes).

Plan (proposed MAP) — target sign + tech kick by 2028-04-12:
1) Today (EOD): Redwood provides pre-flight checklist + sample config (SAML metadata, SCIM uri, ip csv) — Monica
2) 2028-04-04: Procurement & legal review redlines — Clara / Sarah
3) 2028-04-06: Tech discovery (30m) to validate IdP certificate, SCIM credentials, and sample IPs — Monica + Ben + Skyline infra
4) 2028-04-08 to 2028-04-11: Staging cutover window (SCIM initial sync + SSO smoke tests)
5) 2028-04-12: Production rollout + post-go monitoring (1 week)

I’ve attached the SSO metadata and a short checklist to get started. Monica — can you create the MAP doc and confirm who on our side will own the staging cutover (CS vs Solutions)? Ben — please add notes on service account provisioning and any org-policy enforcement caveats.

Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@skylinebank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access gating & procurement checklist for Skyline sandbox

Hi all —

Attached: sso-implementation-checklist.pdf and ip-allowlist-template.csv. I also created a draft MAP in the shared Drive (link below). Key implementation assumptions and asks from our side:

- IdP validation: We need a short window (10–15m) where a Skyline engineer can sign in while we watch logs. Please provide a test account in the engineers group.
- SCIM creds: Please create a service account in your IdP for SCIM with push permissions for groups; provide the bearer token and base URL. If you must use basic auth, note it in the drive doc.
- Rate limits: If you expect >200k users or an enormous org sync, please flag — otherwise the 600 rpm bump request should be sufficient for initial sync.
- IP allowlist: We will stage by environment tags: sandbox (temporary CI range), staging (your QA runners), prod (permanent IPs). Provide a single CSV of ranges per env and we’ll stage them.
- Service accounts: We recommend naming pattern sbx-sa-<team>-<purpose> for sandbox, stg-sa-..., prod-sa-...; attached service-account-naming-guidelines.md.

Next steps I’ll take today: finalize MAP, create the discovery calendar invite for 2028-04-06 10:00 PT, and post the DR checklist for legal/infosec evidence. Ben — can you add a short note on org policies (esp. role inheritance and audit logging) here?

Thanks,
Monica

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SkylineOnboardDocs
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@skylinebank.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access gating & procurement checklist for Skyline sandbox

Hi Clara — quick technical clarifications from the Solutions side. Cutting to the items that most commonly cause rollbacks so the discovery call is focused: 

1) Service accounts and key model:
   - We support short-lived tokens backed by customer-managed KMS for production. For initial staging we can enable long-lived keys but marked as temporary; we’ll rotate them on cutover.
   - Naming: follow Monica’s pattern. We also attach an example IAM policy that limits scope to only the endpoints needed for SCIM provisioning and API calls.

2) SCIM group mapping and membership sync:
   - We recommend mapping by group externalId to avoid duplicates. If Skyline wants two-way group edits we’ll require a controlled window and a sync-back policy to prevent membership thrash.

3) IP allowlist fallback behavior:
   - Staging fallback will be implemented via environment tags. If a request originates from an allowed staging IP, we route to the staging model pool. If it comes from an unauthenticated IP, policy returns 403 with a specific audit code to simplify troubleshooting.

4) Org policies & audit evidence:
   - We will provide: token usage logs (90 days default), admin action audit trail (365 days), and a signed statement for SOC items. If you need extended retention, procurement can add the observability retention add-on.

I’ve added these items to the MAP doc in the drive. Looking forward to the discovery on Friday.

Best,
Ben
--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
